headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: A month of steep losses; the last weeks lean clearly down

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Keep marketing and acquisition budgets at the planned level, but do not step them up: Bitcoin is down about 8% in a week and about 28% in a month, a Rally watch drop window has been open since 13 November, and the headline turns BEARISH if the weakness lasts one more day. Keep a reserve ready instead of cutting, because the long-run base is still rising; spend now on retention, trust and education, and step up acquisition only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($67,733) and then the 200-day average ($72,425). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

Down about 28% over 30 days and about 24% over 90 days.
Fear & Greed is 12 (extreme fear); price is about 13% under its 200-week average.
The 200-day average ($72,425) is still rising, about 5% over 90 days.
watch: The headline still says NEUTRAL, but the medium-term reading has been in its weak zone for four days and turns the headline BEARISH if it stays there one more day. A close back above $61,000 and then $67,733 (the 200-week average) would be the first sign the drop is easing; a close below $57,000 would deepen it.
analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin took another step down, to about $58,927, and fear is extreme, so today is about calm, safety and holding steady, not promotions. Short term, the picture is weak: Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 31 days in a row, sits about 24% below it and about 27% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 12 out of 100. News is pulling this lower: a broad sell-off in tech stocks spread to crypto, and QCP (via PANews) says Bitcoin's weakness reflects that wider market stress more than crypto news, while about $1.54 billion of bets were forced to close in 24 hours. A normal week lately swings about $4,069, so a close above $61,000 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $57,000 (the bottom of it) would turn it down further, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messages fit far better than offers right now.

The next month leans down: the medium-term reading has been in its weak zone for four days, and if it stays there one more day the headline switches from NEUTRAL to BEARISH, while the long-term trend is still up. Price is about 28% lower than 30 days ago and about 24% lower than 90 days ago, and news is nudging this down a little, as a French central bank committee urged the EU to tighten crypto advertising rules and Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade slipped to late January (both PANews). Bitcoin would have to win back $77,127 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed meeting on 8 December is the next scheduled event; keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only barely: the 200-day average is still rising (about 5% over 90 days), yet price is about 19% under it, about 13% under its 200-week average and about 53% below its all-time high. News is adding a little here, as Hong Kong published a bill to bring crypto trading, advice, management and custody under full licensing (PANews). The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,425 (the 200-day average) again; $67,733 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped well under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. More weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and be the time to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
